tagline: The old shore road through Bay St. Louis and Waveland.
intro: Beach Boulevard, once Old Highway 1, keeps to the Hancock County shore for thirteen miles, from Cedar Point at the north tip of Bay St. Louis, across US 90, through the town's historic district and on through Waveland to the fishing village of Bayou Cadet.

The state tells it as the story of a coastal town and its dealings with the water, from seafood for local tables and for export to Buccaneer State Park. Hurricane Katrina came ashore in 2005 at the mouth of the Pearl River, just west of here.

moments.title: Bay St. Louis
moments.text: The town keeps the former Customs House, which processed immigrants into the area, and a Pirate's House said to have links with Jean Lafitte.

moments.title: Waveland
moments.text: The town was nearly destroyed by Camille in 1969, spent nearly a decade recovering, and took the eyewall of Katrina head on in 2005.

moments.title: Buccaneer State Park
moments.text: Andrew Jackson once owned land on Jackson Ridge, and much of the ridge became this Gulf-side park, rebuilt from scratch after Katrina took every building in it.
